thread.title_full: Senator DeWitte urges focus on affordability ahead of governor's budget address

author: N. A. Naylor
title: Senator DeWitte urges focus on affordability ahead of governor's budget address
text:
Senator Don DeWitte and fellow Senate Republicans are urging Governor JB Pritzker to prioritize affordability for Illinois families as the governor prepares to deliver his annual budget address this Wednesday. The group is calling for a responsible, sustainable budget that avoids new or increased taxes and fees.
“Families are already struggling with the rising cost of living. The last thing working people need is a budget that expands government while piling on higher costs,” DeWitte said.
This appeal comes after Democratic lawmakers passed what was described as the largest spending plan in Illinois history last year. The previous budget, which did not receive any Republican votes, included nearly $1 billion in new tax increases and relied on one-time revenue sources. State spending has risen by almost 40 percent since Governor Pritzker took office, with last year’s plan totaling more than $55 billion—a nearly $15 billion increase over prior years.
DeWitte stated, “Our caucus opposed the plan, pointing to record spending, misplaced priorities, a lack of transparency, and a growing financial burden on families and businesses.”
He added: “With the governor set to outline his next budget proposal, I am calling for relief for Illinois citizens. Governor Pritzker needs to rein in spending growth, provide real relief for working families, and commit to a budget that prioritizes taxpayers, families, and businesses, without any new or increased taxes.”
Governor Pritzker will present his annual address before members of the General Assembly at noon on February 18.
In addition to focusing on state finances, Senator DeWitte announced he is co-sponsoring legislation aimed at protecting low-income seniors from losing property tax relief due to inflation. Senate Bill 4029 would tie income eligibility caps for the Low-Income Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Homestead Exemption to inflation starting in tax year 2029. This adjustment would prevent seniors from losing eligibility as their incomes rise with cost-of-living increases.
DeWitte explained: “During the fall veto session, I supported successful legislation that increased the income caps for the senior assessment freeze. Under the new law, the income cap for the senior assessment freeze is set at $75,000 for tax year 2026, $77,000 for 2027, and $79,000 beginning in 2028. SB 4029 would ensure that starting in 2029, the income threshold automatically adjusts each year based on inflation.” He noted that Senate Bill 4029 is currently awaiting assignment to a Senate committee.
For those preparing their taxes ahead of April’s filing deadline, several community programs across Illinois are offering free assistance to low-to-moderate income families, seniors and individuals with disabilities. These include IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA), Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE), AARP Tax-Aide Program, Ladder Up Tax Assistance and GetYourRefund Program. Eligibility varies by program.
“I encourage taxpayers who qualify to review their options and use trusted assistance sites if they need help,” DeWitte said.
Taxpayers can find more information through the Illinois Department of Revenue website or by contacting its taxpayer assistance hotline at 800-732-8866.
DeWitte has represented Illinois’ 33rd Senate District since being elected in 2018; he succeeded Karen McConnaughay in this role.
